name: MAGIC
aliases: Major Atmospheric Gamma Imaging Cherenkov Telescopes

facility_roles.quote: started operations in its final configuration in October 2003

intervals.label: MAGIC-I operations
intervals.quote: The 17 m MAGIC Cherenkov telescope for gamma ray astronomy between 30 and 300 GeV started operations in its final configuration in October 2003

intervals.label: MAGIC-II inauguration / commissioning
intervals.quote: MAGIC became recently a stereoscopic Cherenkov observatory with the inauguration of its second telescope, MAGIC-II, which is currently approaching the end of its commissioning stage.
intervals.note: Exact inauguration month not stated; end date is the December 2009 date of the paper describing commissioning as nearly complete.

intervals.label: stereoscopic operations (MAGIC-I + MAGIC-II)
intervals.quote: MAGIC became recently a stereoscopic Cherenkov observatory with the inauguration of its second telescope, MAGIC-II
intervals.note: Exact month of the start of stereoscopic operations is not stated; 2009 is taken from the paper describing MAGIC-II's inauguration and near-complete commissioning.

intervals.label: camera and readout upgrade
intervals.quote: During summer 2011 and 2012 it underwent a series of upgrades, involving the exchange of the MAGIC-I camera and its trigger system, as well as the upgrade of the readout system of both telescopes.

quantity.quote: MAGIC is a system of two Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes located in the Canary island of La Palma, Spain

summary.plain: Two 17-metre telescopes on a mountain in the Canary Islands that catch the faint blue flashes gamma rays make when they hit the atmosphere.
summary.technical: Imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope system on La Palma, Canary Islands, Spain: MAGIC-I (17 m) operating since October 2003, joined by the stereoscopic MAGIC-II telescope (inaugurated, commissioning nearly complete by December 2009), with a camera/readout upgrade in summer 2011-2012.
